speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: asked the Minister for Finance on how Temasek Holdings and the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation have performed in terms of investment returns over the long term.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: This growth is underpinned by their investment performance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Temasek reports its returns in nominal terms, that is, without taking into account inflation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: I should emphasise that these figures are as at 31 March 2017.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Both entities will be releasing updated numbers for the period ended 31 March 2018 soon.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Temasek and GIC's investments benefit Singaporeans through the Net Investment Return Contribution (NIRC) to the annual Budget.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: The NIR framework allows the Government to spend up to 50% of the long-term expected returns from our Reserves.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: It has become an increasingly important fiscal resource.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: From financial year (FY) 2009 to FY2017, the NIRC totalled about $85 billion, or about 14% of overall revenues.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Eighty-five billion dollars is a sizeable amount that can fund many Government projects and schemes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: It is now the single largest source of Government revenues, larger than any single tax, including the Goods and Services Tax (GST) and corporate and personal tax.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: Our Reserves are an endowment that belongs to Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: There are very few countries in the world which have national savings that they can tap on to fund their budgets, and this is especially rare for a country like Singapore which has no natural resources.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: This endowment was saved over time through the hard work and discipline of our forefathers, invested by GIC and Temasek for the long term.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
text: If we continue to be disciplined and responsible stewards of this endowment, our Reserves will continue to benefit all Singaporeans, young and old, today and tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister share: (a) whether the planned GST increase is linked to past investment losses, such as UBS, Barclays and Merrill Lynch; and (b) can we expect GIC and Temasek to sustain these levels of performance and returns, going forward?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: To be even more specific, if the question is whether the planned GST increase is to cover losses from investments into these or other counters, the answer is also no.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The nature of all investments, whether by Government, sovereign wealth funds, or otherwise, is that you are taking a calculated assessment in the present on the performance of an asset in the future.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It would be wonderful if we had a crystal ball that allows us to see into the future and can accurately predict all investment outcomes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is not possible to guarantee that all investments will make money all of the time.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The only way to avoid any investment loss is just to sit tight and not invest our Reserves, but that would not help either.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Because if we just leave the Reserves as they are and do not invest them, not only will those Reserves not grow, but they will be eroded over time by inflation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we invest, and that means taking some risks and accepting some losses.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But the overall objective is to reap more than you lose over the long term.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: GIC and Temasek have both made money over the long term and have contributed significant revenues to our budget over the years through the NIR framework, as explained earlier.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, one may ask, "Well, if GIC and Temasek contribute to the NIRC, then would not any losses also affect our revenues?" As to this, the NIR framework spending formula is based on expected long-term real returns.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is driven by an overall portfolio approach, taking into account the long-term expected returns of different asset classes, factoring in the diversification benefits, and adjusting based on the long-term investment outlook.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: From this perspective, the outcome of individual investments or the state of markets from one year to the next do not have a significant impact on our spending levels.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, in short, investment outcomes in UBS and so on have not had a significant impact on our revenues.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is designed to smooth out the highs and the lows of investment returns, and to give stability to our fiscal planning.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The need for the GST increase was explained in the 2018 Budget Statement.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And it is really because we have to prepare for the future.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have enough for this decade, but in the next decade 2020 to 2030, our expenditure needs will grow.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We have to plan ahead to meet those needs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We are already reinforcing prudent spending by constraining the growth of Ministry budgets.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We already planned to save ahead and borrow for long-lived capital investments which are enjoyed mainly by future generations.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But even with these measures, there will still be a gap.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And this is because our healthcare, security and other social needs will continue to grow.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This would involve recurrent expenditure for broad-based needs that benefit each generation and should, in principle, be supported by recurrent and broad-based taxes so that each generation pays for its own spending sustainably.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On the Member's second question of whether we can expect GIC and Temasek to sustain this kind of level of performance or returns going forward, there are near-term challenges, such as the current tensions over trade which can affect global economic growth and the investment outlook.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But as I have mentioned, such ups and downs are part and parcel of investing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What is important is that we do not take the creditable investment performance by GIC and Temasek so far for granted.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Government will continue to focus on their long-term overall performance and remain prudent and responsible in how we use our Reserves.
